processing_steps_notes.value: One of a series of 300 °C anneals of different durations applied to the (111)-oriented Fe-16%Al monocrystal for the microhardness study (Fig. 1). unmapped_findings: For the Fe-16%Al monocrystal, the 300 °C/6 h anneal produces the same hardness as the as-grown monocrystal and corresponds to an intermediate degree of short-range order — between the minimum ordering after quenching from 1100 or 600 °C and the maximum ordering after a 250 °C/14-day anneal (b0050).

The hardness of the Fe-16%Al monocrystal does not depend sensitively on heat treatment: the Fig. 1 data vary by only about 10% at most around ~2000 N/mm², and no major impact of short-range ordering on hardness was found (b0029, b0050, figure_001).
No carbides were detected in the Fe-16%Al monocrystal with 45 ppm C after a heat treatment of 14 days at 320 °C, and without heat treatment no carbides were found in all monocrystals (b0026).
Short heat treatments at temperatures up to 300 °C (including 300 °C/6 h) were performed in an argon atmosphere of 99.99% purity, whereas other heat treatments used evacuated SiO2 capsules (b0015).
